## Findings

- [ ] **[Protection/WARN] `ios-build` check is not required on `main`**
  - **Status quo:** The ruleset "main protection" (id 19039316) requires only `test` and `swift-62-build`. The `ios-build` job in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` was added as the regression guard for #44 (iOS platform declaration) but is not a required context — a PR can merge while `ios-build` is red, re-opening exactly the failure mode #44 fixed. Verified: ruleset `required_status_checks` = `[test, swift-62-build]`; HEAD check-runs also report `ios-build`, `Analyze (Swift)`, `Analyze (GitHub Actions)`.
  - **Proposed solution:** Add `ios-build` to the ruleset's `required_status_checks` (`gh api repos/danieljustus/symaira-appkit/rulesets/19039316 -X PATCH` with the extended `required_status_checks` parameters, or via the repo Settings → Rules UI).
  - **Effort/Impact:** Low effort / high impact.

- [ ] **[Protection/WARN] Legacy classic branch protection coexists with the ruleset and is weaker**
  - **Status quo:** `gh api repos/danieljustus/symaira-appkit/branches/main/protection` returns an active classic rule (PR reviews count 0, `dismiss_stale_reviews: false`, `enforce_admins: false`, no conversation resolution, no required status checks) alongside the newer ruleset "main protection" which enforces the stricter real policy. Two overlapping mechanisms are confusing to audit and drift apart over time.
  - **Proposed solution:** Remove the legacy classic branch protection rule and keep the ruleset as the single mechanism (rulesets already apply to `main` with the stricter settings). Verify afterwards that `branches/main/protection` returns 404 and the ruleset still reports `enforcement: active`.
  - **Effort/Impact:** Low effort / medium impact.

- [ ] **[Community/WARN] Issue-template contact link points to disabled GitHub Discussions**
  - **Status quo:** `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/config.yml` links "Symaira Community" to `https://github.com/danieljustus/symaira-appkit/discussions`, but `hasDiscussionsEnabled` is `false` — the contact link is dead for issue reporters.
  - **Proposed solution:** Either enable Discussions on the repo, or remove the `contact_links` entry (keeping `blank_issues_enabled: false`) so users are routed only to the issue forms.
  - **Effort/Impact:** Low effort / medium impact.

- [ ] **[Release/WARN] Documented tag scheme `vX.Y.Z` diverges from actual tags `X.Y.Z`**
  - **Status quo:** `AGENTS.md` (Release section) instructs "Tag `vX.Y.Z` on main", but all releases since 0.6.0 use unprefixed tags (`0.9.2`, `0.9.1`, ...); only old tags `v0.2.2`/`v0.2.3` carry the `v` prefix. Consumers pin `exact: "0.9.2"` (see README Usage), so the unprefixed scheme is the de-facto standard.
  - **Proposed solution:** Update `AGENTS.md` to document the actual scheme (tag `X.Y.Z` without prefix). Optionally re-tag nothing — history is fine; only the doc is wrong.
  - **Effort/Impact:** Low effort / low impact.

## Conclusion

The repo is in very good shape: security features, CI hardening, labels and releases are all correctly configured. Top fixes by impact: (1) require the `ios-build` status check so the #44 regression guard actually gates merges, (2) retire the legacy classic branch-protection rule in favor of the ruleset, (3) fix the dead Discussions contact link in the issue templates.

Note: prior `audit/`, `review/`, `coverage/`, `prerelease/` reports under `.github/` are tracked in git in this repo (deviation from the default local-artifact convention) — kept as-is; report files follow the established repo convention.
